info.title: YBots
info.description: Generated from server/src/api-contract.ts by scripts/api/generate.mjs. Do not edit. Rules: docs/api-contract.md.

get.description: Which apps this server still works with (app-support.ts). Needs no sign-in, so an app can check before it signs in. `updateUrl` is where to get a newer app, when the server is told (ANDROID_UPDATE_URL).

post.description: Answer an approval card, bound to the card by its `digest`. Only a person can (code agent_session).

get.description: Every bot, group and side chat the sign-in may see, with what each is doing now.

post.description: Stop the chat's running turn, or in a group one `member`'s. `stopped` names who was stopped.
Send a message (or, with `editOf`, change one). `clientId` names the send: sending it again after a dropped connection answers the row already there with `duplicate`.

get.description: One Page, with the chat its buttons send into.

post.description: Change a Page: each op answers in `results`, in order.

get.description: A chat's rows, newest last: the latest `limit`, or the `limit` rows before `beforeSeq`.

post.description: Add an emoji to a message, or take it off again (`added` false).

get.description: A bot's side chats. `allowed` false (with `why`) when this bot cannot have them.

post.description: Start a side chat, with an optional title.

delete.description: Delete a task. `removed` is the whole task, for Undo.

patch.description: The person changes a task's title, note or state.

post.description: Undo a task's delete: send back the `removed` task.

get.description: Everything waiting on the person across every bot (needs-you.ts).

patch.description: Switch a routine on or off, or set "post only when something is found". Send at least one.

delete.description: Delete a side chat. It can be brought back (restore) until `undoUntil`.

patch.description: Rename a side chat. Answers the bot's side chats after the change.

schema.description: GET /api/events: a text/event-stream of these, one JSON object per `data:` line, each with an `id:` the app sends back (Last-Event-ID or ?after=) to get what it missed. Apps ignore a `type` they do not know.

ApiError.description: What a refused or failed call answers (4xx, 5xx). `code` names a refusal an app can act on.

ApprovalAnswer.description: An approval card after it was answered (agent/loop.ts approvalReadback).

chatColor.description: The bot's colour in chats (chat-colors.ts): its name, bar and bubble tint where it posts in another bot's chat or a group. Null for a group. `chatColorAuto` = picked for it, not set in settings.

avatarImageUrl.description: A picture that replaces the shape (GET it with the session), or null for the shape.

avatarPoses.description: Pictures of the bot's character in each pose (avatar-poses.ts), made from its picture. Empty for a shape.

avatarPoseJob.description: Making the poses: 'making' while it runs; done/total count the poses.

kind.description: 'room' = group chat (members answer instead of the bot itself).

outside.description: Set for an outside member (outside.ts): it lives elsewhere and is reached through a link.

waitingFor.description: Messages this bot or group sent to an outside member that are still waiting for an answer.

ownerHidden.description: Hidden from the owner's own view (Alex hid a bot): apps leave it out of the home list, pickers and unread counts, and the server sends no notifications about it to the main profile. The bot works as before (other bots and groups still reach it, it stays on the team), and a scoped sign-in (Sam) never sees this as true.

visuals.description: How often it uses answer views, calculators, tap choices and Pages (visuals-level.ts). Not on a group.

busySend.description: What a message sent while it works does (steer-mode.ts): steer (default), queue or interrupt.

webSearch.description: Searches the web and reads pages by API (web-search.ts); off = no web_search/web_extract. Not on a group.

phoneActions.description: May set timers and alarms in the phone's Clock app (phone.ts). Not on a group.

voice.description: Voice chat settings: xAI voice id, speed multiplier (0.7–1.5), BCP-47 language or 'auto'.

model.description: Hermes engine: model id and provider for this bot; null = the engine's default.

modelMode.description: 'auto' = each turn picks a tier from modelTiers by how hard it looks (server/src/model-router.ts).

providerLock.description: When set, the bot never runs on another provider.

sideChats.description: Its side chats (side-chats.ts), when it has any: how many, unread replies in them, and how many are working now.

lastPreview.description: The list's line under the name: whole sentences, never cut mid-text (list-preview.ts).

previewShort.description: The same line in at most 48 characters, for rows too narrow for lastPreview.

previewForms.description: Every whole form of the line, longest first (lastPreview ... previewShort); apps show the first that fits.

previewBy.description: Who the line is about: the bot's own words, a group member's, you or another sender, a card, an event, or an AI summary.

BusySend.description:
What a message you send while a bot is still working on its reply does, set per bot (and per group) in its settings ("While it's working"). Alex asked for steering as the default on 2026-11-24.

 - steer: the message joins the reply being worked on. It is handed to the bot's Hermes at the next safe    point (after the tool step it is on; Hermes' own mid-turn steering, agent.steer), and the bot is told it    is a note about the task in hand. If the reply ends before the bot reaches a safe point, the message    simply becomes the next turn. Nothing is stopped and approval cards stay open.  - queue: the message waits until the reply is finished and then starts a turn of its own (the old    behaviour). An open approval card expires, as before.  - interrupt: the reply being worked on is stopped (like Stop) and the message starts a new turn.

Stop works the same in every mode. A steering message is never an approval of anything.

tools.description: Every tool this card asks about; "Always allow" covers exactly these. Absent on older cards.

digest.description: Hash of what this card shows; a client sends it back with its answer (absent on older cards).

canAlways.description: "Always allow" is offered (the card lists what it covers; allow-rules.ts). Absent on older cards.

lowRisk.description: No listed tool is in a risky class. Notifications offer Allow/Deny only on these.

risk.description: The risky class of a listed tool (shell, files, delete, message, money, host, install, browser, computer, schedule).

alwaysNote.description: A one-line warning for a risky tool, shown next to "Always allow".

canConversation.description: "Allow for this conversation" is offered (conversation-allows.ts): wherever "Always allow" is, but mail, calls, browser cards and plans.

convOff.description: When the person turned off what this card allowed for the conversation (the line above the message box).

kind.description: The kind of action (action-kinds.ts: delete, send, share, post, pay, credentials), its short name and what it does.

handoff.description: A hand-off: the person does it themselves (a password change on a website). "I did it myself" / "Don't do it".

answeredBy.description: Who answered, and from where ("web", "Windows app", "phone app", "voice call"). Absent on older cards.

mail.description: Set on an email send (allow-rules.ts isMailSend): the whole email, shown in full. The card's Send is "allow"; it never offers "Always allow" and cannot be answered from a notification.

sendResult.description: What the real send returned after Send was pressed.

secret.description: A secure input card (browser-cards.ts): the person types a password, code or card detail into a masked box and the server types it into this field of the bot's browser. The value is never on the card.

purchase.description: A purchase card (browser-cards.ts): what the checkout page shows, read by the server, not the bot.

screenHelp.description: A needs-you card: a CAPTCHA, passkey or app approval the person does on the bot's screen.

vault.description: A saved-login card (vault.ts): the owner's Sign in types a saved login into the bot's page. No values.

postingPlan.description: A posting plan card (posting.ts): every day's video, cover and posts, with a switch per day. The answer carries the days left on (routes.ts /approvals/:id/plan).

pluginId.description: The plugin that made it, and its name as the owner knows it.

view.description: Validated data only (plugins/ui-schema.ts); the apps render it, nothing in it runs.

draftId.description: A bot's plan for a new plugin (plugins/builder.ts). Only the owner's Build starts it.
The checked draft. Install sends `digest` back; only the owner can, and never by voice.

intent.description: A bot offering new looks for itself (avatars.ts). Nothing changes until the owner picks one; the bot cannot choose. Pictures are served from /api/bots/:id/look/:candidateId.

resumes.description: How many times drawing was started again after a server restart (avatars.ts resumeLookWork).

files.description: Files a turn wrote in the bot's workspace (files.ts changedSince); each opens in the file pane.

candidateId.description: The chosen picture (a candidate id), shown big with a share button and follow-up ideas.

fromBotId.description: A group member proposing a group skill after working on something together (rooms.ts). Nothing is saved until a person presses Save; a bot cannot answer this card.

skillId.description: The saved skill's id (skills table, bot_id = the group).

title.description: An answer view (views.ts): tables, charts, picks, forms and checklists a bot puts in its reply. Data only; the apps draw it. A press or a Send posts a chat message as the person, so it is never an approval.

text.description: The same content as markdown, for previews, voice, other bots and apps that cannot draw it.

from.description: Set when a group member posted it.

viewId.description: The id the bot uses to change this view later (update_view), and when it last did.

pagePath.description: The Page a person made from it (Open as Page), in the bot's workspace.

quick.description: Choice buttons (choices.ts): one choice block drawn as a row of buttons under the reply, no card around it. `auto` when the server spotted the question rather than the bot offering them.

checkin.description: Check-in offer (checkin-offer.ts): the choice buttons offer to keep an eye on `subject`, and a tap makes a quiet routine for the bot instead of posting a chat message. Never an approval.

pin.description: Pinned board (board-pin.ts): kept in reach above the message box until it is done or let go.

ChatFile.description: A file in a bot's workspace; `path` is relative to the workspace.

screens.description: One screen per bot on the shared computer. width/height are the screen's pixel size.

maxScreens.description: How many bots can have their own screen at once.

call.description: voice-call only: the call record (set on the end-of-call row).

FileKind.description: How the file pane shows a file (server/src/files.ts). 'office' = Word/PowerPoint pages, 'sheet' = spreadsheet tables.

id.description: The model id, or null when the engine's own default answers.

tier.description: Auto mode's tier for this turn; null in manual mode.

fallback.description: True once Hermes moved this turn to a fallback model.

caption.description: Short one-line recap of the model's live reasoning, shown next to "Thinking" (caption.ts). Never cut mid-sentence.

captionFull.description: The whole thought behind `caption`, shown when the person expands the bubble. Null when it says no more.

steps.description: Tool calls made so far in the current turn.

members.description: Group chats only (agent/room-runs.ts): the members answering the group's messages right now. queued: waiting behind other work; working: on it; waiting: one of its approval cards needs you.

model.description: The model answering the current turn and its reasoning effort (model-badge.ts), shown as a small badge on the bot's picture while it works. It follows the model actually used: when Hermes falls back to another model mid-turn this changes and `fallback` is set. Null when idle.

to.description: Who an outside member's message went to (shown "Sheldon to Leonard" in Sheldon's own chat).

from.description: Set when a message came from another bot, a routine, a voice call, or a program signed in to the account ('agent': a Claude thread, a test script) rather than the user typing.

reactions.description: Emoji reactions (reactions.ts). A reaction is feedback only, never an approval of anything.

editedTo.description: On a message you edited (message-edit.ts): the seq of its new version, shown "Edited".

editOf.description: On the new version of a message you edited: the seq of the earlier one.

attachments.description: Pictures and files sent with the message (chat-extras.ts): saved in the bot's Library under uploads/.

steer.description: A message sent while the bot was working, taken into the reply in progress (steer-mode.ts): 'pending' until the bot reaches a safe point, 'read' once handed to it, 'next' when the reply ended first and the message became the next turn. Shown as a small "Steering" marker.

handoff.description: A handoff between bots (bot-handoffs.ts). 'ask': the task as the answering bot's chat shows it. 'answer': the answering bot's reply, written word for word into the asking chat under its name (`from`). Shown "Answer to <askedBy>'s handoff" (kind 'mention': "Answer to your

id.description: Stable for as long as the item waits: `<chatId>:<seq>` for a card, `task:<id>` for a task.

label.description: A short word for the kind, shown as the row's tag ("Approval", "Question", "Stalled").

title.description: What is waiting, in a line.

detail.description: A second line when there is one (the email's subject, the task's last note).

botId.description: The bot (or group) whose list row this belongs to, and the chat the card is in (a side chat's own id).

seq.description: The card's row in the open conversation; absent for a task.

taskId.description: A task's id, for a task or stalled row (they open the bot's tasks).

sideTitle.description: The side chat's title, when the card is in one.

tag.description: One per thing: a new notice with the same tag replaces the old one on every app.

title.description: The chat a tap opens: the bot, or the group a message was posted in.

seq.description: Row to scroll to when the chat opens.

silent.description: Shown with no sound or vibration (quiet hours).

catchUp.description: Missed while the app was away; shown quietly.

approval.description: Only on a low-risk approval card (lowRisk true): Allow and Deny right in the notification.

choices.description: Choice buttons (choices.ts): up to three answers as notification buttons. A tap sends the same pick the chat's buttons send (POST /bots/:chat/cards/:seq/view): a chat reply, never an approval.

chatId.description: Set when it is about one of the bot's side chats: a tap opens that side chat (an older app opens the main chat).

sender.description: Who it is from: the bot that wrote the message (in a group, the member who posted), so apps can show that bot's face. `face` is its face-centred picture (changes address when the picture changes), or null for a bot with no picture, which apps draw as its initial on `color`.

room.description: A group message: the group itself (its name and picture), for the conversation's own picture.

Notice.description: One notification (notify.ts). Same shape on every app: Android, web and Windows.

PageAnswer.description: GET /api/bots/:id/pages?path= : the Page, the chat its buttons send into (page-shelf.ts shelfInfo) and whether it is pinned.

rev.description: The page version of this block's last change, and who made it.

alt.description: A person's edit that arrived after someone else changed the block, waiting to be picked.

PageBlock.description: One block of a Page. Its content fields depend on `type` (see pages.ts `content`).

PlanDayOnCard.description: One day on a posting plan card (posting.ts). Files are the bot's own, read by the server.

PluginBlock.description: What a plugin may show in the apps, as data. Shared by the server (which validates it) and every app (web imports it as

expires.description: End of the last day, epoch ms, in `tz`.

PostingPlanOnCard.description: A posting plan card: days with posts; `result` once answered (the days approved).

botSays.description: What the bot said it is buying (its words).

warnings.description: Plain warnings: totals differ, nothing read, recurring charge.

result.description: After Approve: armed (the bot may place the order within 3 minutes), or why not.

PurchaseOnCard.description: A checkout as the purchase card shows it (browser-cards.ts). Everything under `page` was read from the page.

Reaction.description: Who reacted: a person on the account, or a Bot (by id).

RemovedTask.description: A task the person deleted, whole, so the app's Undo can put it back exactly (POST /bots/<id>/tasks/restore).

quiet.description: Post only when something is found: a run with nothing to report leaves no message in the chat.

failCount.description: Failed runs in a row, and the last one's error (routines.ts, the fatigue rule).

autoOffAt.description: Set when it switched itself off after 10 failures in a row; cleared when it is turned back on.

Row.description: A transcript row. `seq` orders rows; `updatedSeq` is a per-bot revision counter (rows are rewritten while streaming).

origin.description: The page's own origin (https://accounts.example.com) and its host for big type.

frameOrigin.description: Set when the field is inside a frame from another origin (a card iframe).

fieldLabel.description: The field's label as the page shows it.

why.description: What the bot said it is for (its words; shown as such).

masked.description: Shown masked; one-time codes and usernames may be shown as typed.

numeric.description: Digits only (codes, card numbers): the apps show a number pad.

canSave.description: The card offers "Save to my logins" (vault.ts): a sign-in field on a page saved logins can fill.

result.description: After Fill: filled, or why not. Never the value. `saved` when it was also saved to the person's logins.

SecretOnCard.description: The field a secure input card is for (browser-cards.ts).

SideChat.description: One of a bot's side chats (side-chats.ts): a conversation of its own with the same bot, beside its main chat. Its rows, live state and cards are read and sent with `id` like any chat (/bots/<id>/rows, /bots/<id>/messages, /bots/<id>/interrupt...); the bot it belongs to is `botId`.

stale.description: Marked "working" but untouched for hours while its bot is idle (store.ts taskStale).

screenshot.description: Data URL thumbnail for computer actions.

origin.description: The page's own origin and host, read from the browser.

frameOrigin.description: Set when the fields are inside a frame from another origin.

login.description: The saved login: its id, the site it was saved for, its label and a username hint ("a•••@example.com").

fields.description: What will be typed, and the page's own labels for those fields.

owner.description: Whose login it is (first name), and whether that is a scoped sign-in (only that sign-in can press Sign in).

connectorFirst.description: A mail, calendar or money site: the bots use connected apps there first.

why.description: What the bot said it is for (its words).

result.description: After Sign in: which fields were filled, or why not.

VaultOnCard.description: A saved-login card (vault.ts, browser-cards.ts useSavedLogin). Never carries a username or password.

ViewBlock.description: One piece of an answer view. Its fields depend on `type` (views.ts VIEW_TYPES). `sentAt` marks a sent choice, form or button.

VisualsLevel.description:
How often a bot reaches for answer views, calculators, tap choices and Pages, set per bot in its settings ("Visuals in replies"). It only changes the guidance in the bot's prompt (agent/prompt.ts and the group brief in agent/rooms.ts); the tools stay available at every level.

This is separate from the app's own "Answer visuals: Rich / Simple" switch, which only changes how a device draws views that arrive (Simple shows them as text). That one is per device; this one is per bot.

The text must not depend on the clock: it sits in the cached part of the prompt.
